blocks.label: Raise a defence after a resisted hit, a few times per entry
blocks.summary: After a damaging hit that my typing resists (but does not block), I gain 1 stage of Defense if it was physical, else Sp. Def. At most 2 times per switch-in, once per foe move.
examples: After a not very effective hit, raise Defense or Sp. Def by 1, up to 2 times per entry

params.label: Stat raised after a physical move
Stat raised after a special or other damaging move

feasibility: The hit must really deal damage and must not be blocked or fully immune (checked inside the class until the librarian adds those conditions)
I can gain only a limited number of boosts per switch-in, and a multi-hit move counts once (a private counter inside the class)
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only. The trigger (after I am hit) and the resisted-hit condition (two move.effectiveness atoms bound in bindings.ts) are separate and swappable. Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: it raises a stat that is chosen by the incoming move's category (physical: one stat, otherwise another) and it updates a private counter and a once-per-foe-move memory; effect.stat-stage has one fixed stat and no memory, so staff would need an effect with a 'stat that matches the hit's category' choice (requested as R-B13-15). The guards (damage dealt, not blocked) and the residual (counter below the cap, new foe move) stay in the class and are listed under 'also requires'; requests R-B13-3, R-B13-4, R-B13-6 and R-B13-14 add the atoms. Review of the numbers: the cap (2), the stages (1) and the two stats (Defense, Sp. Def) were literals; they are now trailing constructor arguments with the old values as defaults and are params. Users: Anneal (5979, attr 1). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) apply bumps the counter and stores the move record even when simulated (only the stat change is skipped); the harness never simulates PostDefend. (2) The effectiveness gate calls getMoveEffectiveness twice (kept as it was). (3) A resisted move that is 'immune' is excluded by the second clause (effectiveness > 0). (4) The ability text says the raise is for a physical move or a special move; a damaging status-category hit cannot occur, so the 'other' stat only ever follows a special move.

blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE, justified: the effect is the reset of a private per-Pokemon record (the raise count and the last counted foe move) that only AnnealAbAttr reads; the library has no 'counter' memory block to express a reset of (requested as `effect.reset-memory`, R-B13-23, the generalised R-B13-9 effect.reset-charges, in requests/B13.md). It is a single assignment, so there is nothing further to split. The trigger is a normal switch-in WHEN and the class has no condition. Users: Anneal (5979, attr 0). ODDITY (not fixed): apply ignores `simulated`, so a simulated PostSummon call would reset the counter; no engine path simulates PostSummon today.

blocks.label: Drain a foe move's PP and store a charge when I hit
blocks.summary: When my damaging move hits, the foe's last-used move (or a random one) loses 1 PP and I store a charge, up to 3. Stored charges power up my draining moves.
examples: Each time I land a hit, take 1 PP from the move the foe used last

params.label: PP taken from the foe's move

feasibility: The foe must have a move with PP left to drain
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only. The trigger (after my hit) and every condition are separate: the attack condition is a real constructor slot bound to move.damaging, the other three clauses are the gate (legacy-closure, requests in requests/B13.md). Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: it drains one PP from a foe move that is chosen by a remembered per-foe name or by a random draw, adds to a private charge counter capped at 3, and remembers the last move record so a multi-hit move counts once. There is no 'drain PP' effect and no 'charge counter' memory block in the library (both requested), and the counter is read by a different place (HitHealAttr), so splitting would re-implement the class. Users: Foul Harvest (5973, attr 0). Review fix: the PP taken (default 1) and the charge cap (default 3) are now trailing constructor arguments (indices 2 and 3, after the base class's attack condition and show-ability) and params; with PP drain 1 the PP update equals the old `ppUsed++` because the move is known to have PP left. The foe-move pick (remembered move, else one random draw) stays fixed inside the package. ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) apply stores lastMoveRecord BEFORE its simulated and empty-moveset checks, so a simulated call or a foe without usable moves still spends the once-per-move memory; (2) the random pick (the only draw) happens before the 'no PP left' check, so a foe whose moves are all out of PP still consumes one draw; (3) the heal bonus lives in HitHealAttr by class name, an engine coupling the decomposition does not see; (4) the ability text says a 'direct hit', but canApply has no direct-hit test beyond the PostAttack dispatch.

If I also carry the Sediment Bloom mark, eating a hazard plants a Sediment Bloom on the foes' side
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only; the trigger (end of turn) and the hazard-on-my-side condition are separate and bound to eight library atoms. Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: it removes ONE layer from the first hazard of a fixed list (a field edit with layers), tells Sediment Bloom about it, and raises TWO stats in a single queued change; the library has no 'remove hazard layers' effect (requested as R-B13-18, which also asks effect.stat-stage to accept a list of stats). Review of the numbers: the layers (1) and the stages (1) were literals, now trailing constructor arguments with the old values as defaults; the layers semantic 'layers > n ? layers -= n : remove' equals the old 'layers > 1 ? layers-- : remove' for n = 1. Users: Glam Rock (5975, attr 1; attr 0 is ForceSwitchOutImmunityAbAttr, the 'cannot be forced out' half, which is another batch's class). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) the gate and the effect each list the hazards separately; FIXED by making the gate non-editable and non-removable, so it cannot disagree with the effect. (2) The effect does nothing when simulated and has no other clause. (3) The Infestation trap is an ER hazard tag, not a vanilla one.

feasibility: A weight class counts how many of the weights 10, 25, 50, 100 and 200 kg a Pokemon has reached (fixed in the class), so 5 is the most classes that can ever differ
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only; the trigger (move power) and the move condition are separate and bound to library atoms. Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: the multiplier is computed from the LIVE weights of the holder and of the target (weight classes, capped), not a constant that effect.multiply-power can hold; requested as R-B13-16 (`effect.multiply-power-by-weight-difference`). Review of the numbers: 10% per class and the cap of 5 were literals, now trailing constructor arguments (defaults reproduce the old maths exactly, 10/100 equals 0.1 in floating point) and params; the five weight thresholds stay fixed in the class. Users: Heavyweight (5982, attr 0) and Meteor Mass (5997, attr 1; its first attr is a weight multiplier of 3 that raises the holder's weight class). The shipped ability text says 'up to 50%': that is maxClasses 5 x 10%. Bound gate: the punching atom move.flag asks doesFlagEffectApply while the class asks move.hasFlag; for PUNCHING_MOVE no ability injects the flag today, so the two agree (L1 compares them over the grid). ODDITIES (not fixed): apply has no side effects, so simulated calls make no difference. The ability text promises 'weight-based moves' but only Heavy Slam and Heat Crash are included, not Low Kick or Grass Knot.

blocks.label: Store a charge when a foe's hit damages me
blocks.summary: When a foe's move damages me, I store 1 charge, up to 3. A multi-hit move counts once. My next Ground move spends the stored charges for extra power.
examples: Gain 1 stored charge each time a foe's attack damages me, up to 3
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only; the trigger (after I am hit) and the gate are separate. Justified: the effect adds 1 to a private per-Pokemon counter capped at 3 and records which foe move was counted, both read and spent by a different attr (PorousPowerAbAttr). The library has no 'charge counter' memory block (requested in requests/B13.md as `effect.store-charge` / `time.charges`), and `effect.arm-effect` has no stack count or cap, so the effect cannot be split without re-implementing the counter. Review fix: the cap (default 3) is now a constructor argument and a param; the once-per-foe-move memory stays inside the package. Users: Porous (5974, attr 2). ODDITY (not fixed): apply has no `simulated` check, so a simulated PostDefend call would add a charge and queue the message; the L1/L2 harness never simulates PostDefend. The ability text says 'direct hit', but canApply tests only damage > 0 and a landed hit.

blocks.label: Spend stored charges to boost my Ground moves
blocks.summary: My Ground move gains 25% power per stored charge and all charges are spent. Example: 2 charges turn 100 power into 150.
blocks.whenLabel: While the game calculates a move's power

feasibility: I must have at least one stored charge (a private counter, checked inside the class)
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only; the trigger (move power) and the move-type condition are separate and bound to a library atom. Justified: the multiplier is derived from a private counter (1 + 0.25 x charges, not a constant the multiply-power block can hold) and the same effect spends the counter and queues a message; splitting would re-implement the counter. The library has no 'multiply by an amount per stored charge' effect, no 'stored charges' condition and no 'spend charges' effect (requested in requests/B13.md). The 'has a charge' clause stays in the class as the residual (listed under 'also requires') and keeps its original second position. Review fix: the percent per charge (default 25, was a literal) is now a constructor argument and a param; the cap (+75% at 3 charges) follows from the Store-a-charge cap. The multiplier is still computed in the overridden apply as 1 + percent/100 x charges, which is why this stays a package instead of the multiply-power block (R-B13-9). Users: Porous (5974, attr 3). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) apply multiplies power even when simulated but only spends the charges when not simulated (correct for a preview); (2) the base class's multiplier argument (1) is dead because apply is overridden; (3) the boost is computed from the counter AT the time the power is calculated, so a power calculation that is not followed by the real move (a preview that is not marked simulated) would spend charges early.

blocks.label: Plant a draining bloom when I remove a hazard
blocks.summary: When I remove an entry hazard from my side, a Bloom grows on the foes' side. At the end of each turn it drains 1/16 of each foe's max HP and heals my side by the total.
examples: After I clear a hazard, drain a sixteenth of the foes' HP every turn and heal my team

params.label: Drain one Nth of each foe's max HP every turn (N)

feasibility: It only works for hazards removed by me (my own end-of-turn hazard eating, or a hazard-clearing move I use)
The drain and the healing run from the end-of-turn code of the field effect, not from this ability's own moment
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE, justified: the mechanic is spread over three places (the marker, notifyHazardRemovedBy that plants a field effect, processSedimentBlooms that drains and heals at turn end) and has no moment of its own; splitting it would re-implement the field effect. Honest limits: (0) the always-on placeholder is tracked under R-B13-19 (the label says 'when I remove a hazard', the declared WHEN is the placeholder; the marker classes are now listed as while.active flag keys so L0 passes); (1) the trigger is not a library WHEN, so the declaration uses the always-on placeholder and the label says what really happens (R-B13-19 asks for 'When I remove an entry hazard from my side'); (2) the trigger has NO conditions of its own; (3) LIBRARY GAP, L0 will report it: the class extends AbAttr directly, so no WHEN dispatch key is an ancestor of it (while.active lists its flag classes explicitly); R-B13-19 asks the librarian to add the marker classes there. Edit made outside the class (same file): processSedimentBlooms now reads the planter's marker for the divisor (1/16 when the planter is gone or has no marker, which is the old constant). Users: Sediment Bloom (5976, attr 0). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) the planter is found by the tag's source id; if the planter leaves the field its marker is no longer 'active' and the drain falls back to 1/16. (2) The heal goes to EVERY Pokemon on the planter's side for the FULL total (not split). (3) drained counts the HP actually lost, so a foe at 1 HP adds 1.

Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: one effect does TWO multiplications, the second only for two move types, in a single apply (a conditional inside the effect; two effect.multiply-power blocks would be two attrs). The 'face is out' clause stays in the class as the residual (second position, as in the original) and is listed under 'also requires'; request R-B13-22 adds a condition that reads that memory. The ability is unsuppressable, uncopiable and unreplaceable (ability-level flags set by the builder, not by this class). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) the unleash memory is written by prepareTwoFacedMove/finishTwoFacedMove in move-effect-phase.ts (found by class name), so the effect depends on engine call sites the declaration cannot show; (2) the 'every other turn' timing lives in twoFacedReady, also outside the class; (3) the ability text says 'damage', the class multiplies move power.
